answer.summary: The research question lacks empirical grounding and must be revised to isolate a single, measurable metric from peer-reviewed literature before further analysis can proceed.
answer.content: After two plan reviews, the original research question remains unanswerable due to absence of peer-reviewed evidence on output token coherence or semantic drift under intermittent input with bounded token budgets. A bounded revision is required to focus on a single, verifiable metric such as coherence decay from a controlled study using time-series linguistic embedding models. Without this, comparative analysis and downstream validation cannot proceed with empirical validity.
answer.search: find peer-reviewed study on coherence decay in tokenized agent outputs under intermittent input with bounded token budgets and known perturbations using time-series linguistic embedding models
answer.nextTask: handoff to analyst to extract coherence decay metrics and per-interval drift scores from the identified study
answer.lesson: All research questions involving agent memory must be anchored in a single, verifiable metric from peer-reviewed studies before comparative analysis can proceed; avoid multi-dimensional, ungrounded inquiries in early phases.'
